source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Symptoms limited mainly to the extremities, rather than the neurological changes this condition actually tends to cause","B":"Headache, changes in level of consciousness, and vomiting (sometimes without nausea), among other early findings","C":"An improvement in the client's overall level of consciousness with fairly little other finding noted on assessment","D":"A fairly ordinary, expected finding that would not typically call for any further clinical evaluation"}}
source_row.rationale: Early signs of increased intracranial pressure may include headache, changes in level of consciousness (often one of the earliest and most sensitive indicators), and vomiting (sometimes without preceding nausea), requiring prompt recognition since increased ICP can progress to serious, life-threatening complications.
